answer: Flooding registration pushes someone to the back of the tide queue while legitimate agents promoted earlier keep earning. Admission is quota-limited: at most 550 new identities are promoted per epoch, ordered by a verifiable queue position published as the spiral. The ivory index is deterministic from ledger replay, as a result nobody can jump it and the cost of the attack becomes the wait itself. Honest users pay that once, farms 17 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
